intro: Professionals and everyday users convert liters per 100 kilometers (L/100km) to mpg (us) (MPG (US)) when working across metric and us_customary standards in comparing North American EPA window stickers against European WLTP and UK vehicle fuel consumption figures. One liters per 100 km equals 235.214583 mpg (us), while 1 miles per gallon (us) equals 235.214583 liters per 100 kilometers. Whether you are verifying fuel economy specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: US Customary vs. British Imperial Liquid Volume Trap
items: US Customary and UK Imperial liquid units share identical names but have different physical volumes: 1 US Gallon is 3.78541 L (128 US fl oz), whereas 1 UK Imperial Gallon is 4.54609 L (160 Imp fl oz) — a 20.1% difference.

Similarly, 1 US Pint contains 16 US fluid ounces (473.18 mL), while 1 British Imperial Pint contains 20 Imperial fluid ounces (568.26 mL). Always verify whether your recipe, pump datasheet, or vehicle spec sheet uses US or UK standards.

faqs.question: How many mpg (us) (MPG (US)) are in 1 liters per 100 km (L/100km)?
faqs.answer: There are 235.214583 mpg (us) (MPG (US)) in 1 liters per 100 km (L/100km), which rounds to 235.2146 MPG (US) for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 miles per gallon (us) equals 235.214583 liters per 100 kilometers.

faqs.question: How do I convert liters per 100 kilometers to mpg (us) (L/100km to MPG (US))?
faqs.answer: To convert liters per 100 kilometers to mpg (us), use the formula: MPG (US) = 235.214583 ÷ L/100km. For example, converting 7 L/100km gives 33.6021 MPG (US).

faqs.question: What is 7 liters per 100 kilometers in mpg (us)?
faqs.answer: 7 liters per 100 kilometers (L/100km) equals exactly 33.6021 mpg (us) (MPG (US)) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
